source_text: 62. C'est pourquoi le prophète dit encore: «En ce jour je relèverai la tente de David qui est tombée» (Am 9, 11), c'est-à-dire le corps du Christ, celui qui tire son origine de David, comme nous l'avons dit plus haut; c'est évidemment déclarer qu'après sa mort, le Christ ressuscitera d'entre les morts; son corps est appelé tente. Tous ces témoignages de l'Ecriture établissent donc que le Christ qui, selon la chair, doit être de la race de David, sera le Fils de Dieu, qu'après être mort, il ressuscitera, qu'il aura l'aspect d'un homme, mais aussi la puissance de Dieu. Il jugera lui-même tout l'univers, seul il accomplira la justice et sera sauveur
pass_a_gloss: §62 dual gloss (Armenian-via-French sense) ≠ Pass B running English. Theme: Fallen tent of David = Christ’s body raised.
pass_b_english: Therefore the prophet says again: ‘In that day I will raise up the tent of David that has fallen’ ([[Amos 9:11 >> Bible:Amos 9:11]]; [[Acts 15:16 >> Bible:Acts 15:16]]) — that is, the body of Christ, which draws its origin from David, as we said above. This is clearly to declare that after his death Christ will rise from the dead; his body is called a tent.

All these scriptural witnesses establish, then, that the Christ who according to the flesh is to be of David’s race will be the Son of God; that after dying he will rise; that he will have the appearance of a human being, but also the power of God. He himself will judge the whole universe; he alone will accomplish justice and will be savior. ([[Rom 1:3-4 >> Bible:Rom 1:3-4]]; [[Acts 17:31 >> Bible:Acts 17:31]])
